card.name: Pericon
card.era: Evolved late 18th-early 19th c. from cielito/contradanza; Pericón Nacional registered 1880s
card.tagline: Stately group square-dance of eight couples waving handkerchiefs.
card.profile: The pericón is a group folk dance of Argentina and Uruguay performed by a set of independent couples, generally eight, who execute coordinated contradance/quadrille figures at the shout of '¡Aura!' - including the famous 'pabellón,' where couples raise handkerchiefs to form a flag. Dancers wear colonial-era dress and carry pañuelos (Spanish Wikipedia; Plan Ceibal). It evolved from the cielito (a descendant of the British country dance) alongside the media caña.
card.insight: The pericón was declared the 'Danza Nacional Argentina' by Ley 26.297 (2007); the popular 'Pericón Nacional' score was registered by Gerardo Grasso in the late 1880s (Argentina InfoLeg; Spanish Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: The group star dance with a caller. A representative image shows colorful regional costume and lively partner or troupe footwork — Rio de la Plata, Argentina.
